correctness.rationale: Exact divisor-sum calculation produces the strict inequality p<2^{a+1}, with parity removing equality. Summing primes over a and splitting at 2^{3a+2}=X gives an exact formula. Uniform PNT on fixed multiplicative windows plus geometric-tail bounds yields F(s), and direct differentiation gives both exact extrema; independent divisor-sum checks agree for all 274 candidates up to 250000. The finite regression is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is the first repeated odd-prime-power layer following the dominant p-first-power layer in two-prime divisor-sum phenomena, directly motivated by the preexisting prime-square excedent literature. Determining its exact phase function and sharp nonconstant lower and upper asymptotic limits is a natural sparse-family counting theorem, not a routine numerical extension. It provides no result for arbitrary odd-prime exponents.
